name: Tail risk hedging
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Insurance Against Market Crashes
caseLead: S&P 500 put options can provide substantial protection during sharp equity sell-offs because their value generally rises as the index falls and implied volatility increases. This protection remains costly because severe sell-offs are infrequent, but demand for puts can rise quickly when geopolitical or policy events increase concerns about equity losses.
caseRest: The main cost is the repeated option premium paid during periods without a major market decline. This cost can accumulate for years, so the strategy can lose money in most months before a single sell-off repays it. As a result, the hedge is useful only if the portfolio can tolerate repeated small losses and the premium budget is kept small.
figNote: Each card shows the highest closing level of the VIX during the episode. The VIX measures the volatility that S&P 500 options price in for the next 30 days: it has averaged about 19 over the long run, while readings above 30 signal market stress.

events.title: Lehman failure drives protection prices sharply higher
events.text: The October 2008 sell-off followed the Lehman Brothers failure and a freeze in bank funding, lifting the VIX to an 80 close. The strategy gained because puts bought earlier rose far above their cost as the S&P 500 fell about 17 per cent.

events.title: US credit downgrade lifts the VIX above 45
events.text: The US credit rating downgrade and euro area debt worries lifted the VIX to a 48 close in August 2011. The strategy gained because index puts rose as the S&P 500 fell about 17 per cent within three weeks.

events.title: Fed tapering talk lifts the VIX only briefly
events.text: Signals in June 2013 that the Fed would slow bond purchases lifted bond yields and raised the VIX to a 20 close. The strategy lost because the S&P 500 recovered within weeks, so the puts expired with little value.

events.title: Covid lockdowns drive the VIX to a record
events.text: Covid lockdowns in March 2020 cut the S&P 500 by about 34 per cent in 23 trading days, lifting the VIX to an 83 close. The strategy gained because index puts rose many times in value as the fall far exceeded the premium paid.

events.title: Russia's invasion of Ukraine lifts protection costs
events.text: Russia's February 2022 invasion of Ukraine pushed energy prices higher and lifted the VIX to a 36 close in early March. Results were mixed because the S&P 500 recovered within weeks, so gains on the puts were modest while premiums stayed high.

events.title: US tariff announcement drives the VIX above 50
events.text: Broad US tariffs announced in April 2025 lifted the VIX to a 52 close as the S&P 500 fell about 19 per cent from its high. Results were mixed because the rebound within weeks reduced the value of puts held through it.

instrument: S&P 500 index put options; about three months to expiry; rolled monthly
rules: Puts struck about 10% below the index bought each month within a premium budget; VIX call options added when implied volatility is low
costs: Estimated bid-ask spreads and commissions deducted at each roll
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from premium budget to crash payout

legs.purpose: Pays out in a large fall
Holds the cash reserve and earns the cash rate

entry: Puts bought each month when the premium is within budget
size: Premium capped at 2% of capital a year
exit: Puts sold at 3 times cost or 30 days before expiry
stop: No new puts bought once the annual premium budget is spent
marketWatch: The cost of three month puts relative to recent realised volatility, the VIX term structure and the difference in implied volatility between downside and at-the-money options are key indicators. Scheduled central bank decisions, tariff announcements and elections can raise the likelihood of a large market move. Rehyn watches whether protection is cheap relative to the range of recent index moves.

favourable.heading: Sudden equity sell-offs
favourable.text: Sharp falls in the S&P 500 favour the strategy because put prices rise as the index falls and implied volatility increases. In March 2020 the S&P 500 fell about 34 per cent in 23 trading days and the VIX closed at 83, so index puts rose many times in value.

favourable.heading: Complacent markets before a shock
favourable.text: Low implied volatility before a shock favours the strategy because it makes puts cheaper to buy when a sell-off becomes more likely. In early 2020 the VIX was near 14, so protection cost little before the Covid sell-off.

favourable.heading: Unexpected policy announcements
favourable.text: Unexpected policy announcements favour the strategy because they raise demand for protection before investors can reduce risk. After the April 2025 tariff announcement, the VIX closed at 52 and index puts gained sharply within days.

adverse.heading: Steady rallies in calm markets
adverse.text: A steadily rising market hurts the strategy because puts expire without value while the premium is paid every month. In 2017 the S&P 500 returned about 22 per cent and the VIX closed below 10 on many days, so the premium paid earned nothing.

adverse.heading: Brief spikes that reverse
adverse.text: Short sell-offs hurt the strategy because the S&P 500 recovers before puts gain much value and implied volatility falls back. In August 2024 the VIX closed at 39 on 5 August and fell below 20 within two weeks, so puts bought earlier gave back most of their gain.

adverse.heading: Expensive protection after a shock
adverse.text: High implied volatility after a shock hurts the strategy because new puts cost far more while the market recovers. After the VIX closed at 83 in March 2020, a rolling position paid several times the usual premium to renew as equities rose over the following months.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's return over each event window, measured from the last market high before the shock to the market low using the default backtest parameters above. Positive figures mean the puts paid out during the event.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in the S&P 500 and implied volatility, which are then applied to the strategy's current put and VIX option positions.
